Subject: SignalFlow service-impact briefing & remedial commitments

Hi Michael / SignalFlow team,

First, thank you for your patience while we finished our internal analysis. Attached is a customer-facing RCA draft and the event timeline CSV; we wanted to share our findings and concrete next steps. Short summary up front:

- Incident window: 2027-06-01 01:22:00 UTC — 2027-06-01 03:47:00 UTC
- Impact: elevated generation latency and token truncation affecting ~12% of requests routed to your dedicated pool; no data exfiltration detected.
- Root cause (summary): edge load-balancer misconfiguration combined with an aggressive cache-eviction sequence triggered by a malformed client retry pattern, which exposed a rare race in our KV cache code path.

Key remedial actions we are committing to:
1) Immediate: roll back the recent LB config change (completed 2027-06-01 04:10 UTC).
2) Short-term (2 weeks): deploy a guarded cache-eviction patch and rate-limited retry defense to prevent recurrence.
3) Medium-term (60 days): full audit of retry-handling + engineered observability dashboards for prefix-cache pressure.

Attached: signalflow-incident-rca-draft.pdf (RCA summary), 20270601-event-timeline.csv (chronological events), mitigation-plan-checklist.md (action tracker).

We know these incidents interrupt your product. Marissa from Customer Success is copied to coordinate next steps and any credit/contract questions. Diego and Aditya from Engineering are on the thread for technical follow-ups.

Would you be available for a 30-minute wrap-up call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through the timeline and agree on a fix verification plan? If another time works better, tell us and we'll adjust.

Apologies again, and we appreciate your partnership.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tessa / team — technical summary for Michael below; feel free to paste into the thread.

Short confirmation (to send to SignalFlow):
- Attribution: your traffic was identified by dedicated pool tags and per-customer routing headers. Packet-level sampling and request-id correlation confirmed retries originated from a subset of client-side SDK versions (v1.9.3 and earlier) used by SignalFlow.
- Retry behavior: amplified retries increased prefix churn and triggered an edge->intra-pool cache-eviction loop. That sequence revealed a rare race condition in our KV cache LRU cascade when eviction occurs concurrently with active KV writes.

Owners & dates:
- Short-term patch (guarded eviction + rate-limited retry handler): owner: Diego Fernandez, target: 2027-06-15 UTC (testing environment available 2027-06-10).
- Verification run with SignalFlow: owner: Aditya Rao, target: 2027-06-17 — we will run a controlled load test against a staging variant of your pool and share metrics.
- 60-day audit (retry-handling + observability): owner: Aditya Rao, target: 2027-08-01 deliverable: audit report + dashboards.

Test plan highlights:
- Reproduce amplified retry pattern with recorded production traces (safe, replay-only permissioned test).
- Increase synthetic prefix pressure while monitoring cache hit-rate, eviction logs, and tail-latency.
- If patch passes, perform gradual rollout behind a canary policy for 24h, then full rollout.

Notes: rolling back the LB config was low-risk and already done; the patch is backward-compatible but requires careful canarying because it touches cache control.

Diego
VP, Inference Engineering

Michael — thanks again for the call this morning. Following up with the finalized customer-facing RCA and the confirmed remedial plan. Highlights and next steps (copying the attachments):

1) Root cause (final): an interaction between an LB configuration change and an amplified client retry pattern exposed a race in our KV cache eviction logic. No customer data was read or exported.

2) What we changed and when:
- 2027-06-01 04:10 UTC: rolled back LB config change (mitigated immediate routing pressure).
- 2027-06-02 09:00 UTC: deployed temporary retry-throttle rule at edge (reduced retry amplification by ~90%).
- Planned 2027-06-15 UTC: guarded cache-eviction patch (Diego) — staging testing begins 2027-06-10.

3) Commitments:
- We will run a controlled verification test with your team on 2027-06-17 (Aditya owner).
- We will provide a formal SLA credit statement and the required procurement-ready wording by 2027-06-04 (Marissa owner).
- 60-day audit report and dashboard delivery by 2027-08-01.

4) Attachments: signalflow-incident-rca-draft.pdf (finalized), 20270601-event-timeline.csv, mitigation-plan-checklist.md.

If you'd like, we'll send the credit statement as a signed letter on Redwood letterhead; Marissa will coordinate. Please let us know any specific format procurement needs.

Appreciate the partnership and we'll share progress updates on the HubSpot ticket (SF-8492) and the incident page: https://redwood.app/signalflow/incidents/2027-06-01

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
